body: C.M No.01/2026 This civil miscellaneous application seeks restoration of an application under Section 12(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (“CPC”), dismissed for non-prosecution on 27.05.2025 by the Additional District Judge, Lahore. The proceedings were transmitted to this Court pursuant to letter No.21 dated 02.03.2026, addressed by the Additional District and Sessions Judge, Lahore, to the Director General, Directorate of District Judiciary, Lahore High Court, Lahore, with reference to Section 13(1)(b) of the Punjab Establishment of Special Courts (Overseas Pakistanis Property) Act 2025 (“the Act”).

2. When the matter was initially taken up, learned counsel for the parties sought time to prepare the brief. At the subsequent hearing, learned counsel for the applicant questioned the transfer. He submits that Section 13(1)(b) of the Act concerns appeals and revisions, whereas the transferred proceedings comprise an application under Section 12(2), CPC and an application for its restoration. He maintains that both applications should be decided by the Court which passed the judgment dated 01.10.2019 under challenge, and that their adjudication by this Court would deprive the applicant of a forum of challenge.

3. Learned counsel for respondent No.1 (“the respondent”), the only contesting respondent, submits that both the applicant and the respondent are overseas Pakistanis and supports the transfer. He raises no objection to restoration, while reserving his objections to the maintainability and merits of the application under Section 12(2), CPC. Adds that the applicant must identify and establish the fraud allegedly committed in obtaining the judgment under challenge. Respondent No.2 has already been proceeded against ex-parte. According to the Office report, respondent No.3-Lahore Development Authority has been served through its clerk. As no one has appeared on its behalf, it is also proceeded against ex-parte.

4. Learned Law Officer, appearing on Court’s call, submits that the Act is a beneficial enactment intended to protect the property rights of overseas Pakistanis and that Section 13 of the Act must be construed with reference to the proceedings from which the applications arise.

6. The question is whether an application under Section 12(2), CPC seeking to reopen an appellate judgment, together with an application for its restoration, falls within the appellate allocation under Section 13(1)(b) of the Act. Section 13 of the Act provides as follows.
“13. Transfer of pending cases.– (1) On the commencement of this Act:

(a) all petitions, suits, execution petitions and all other proceedings pending in any other court, in which overseas Pakistani is a party, shall stand transferred to the special court and on transfer of the cases, the special court may proceed with the cases from the stage at which it was pending; and (b) all appeals, revisions, in which any or all the parties are overseas Pakistanis, pending before any court after the commencement of this Act, shall stand transferred to special bench or benches of the concerned High Court for adjudication.”

The statutory scheme establishes an exclusive forum for disputes concerning immovable property involving overseas Pakistanis. In Muhammad Mudassar Iqbal v. The Lake City Holdings Pvt. Ltd. (2026 LHC 2886), this Court held that the application of the Act depends upon the subject matter of the dispute and the overseas Pakistani status of a party. Both requirements are satisfied here. Clauses (a) and (b) must accordingly be read together to identify the forum assigned to the proceedings. Clause (a) provides for transfer to the Special Court, while clause (b) allocates appeals and revisions to the Special Bench of this Court. The application under Section 12(2), CPC challenges the final appellate judgment dated 01.10.2019. The applicant alleges that she neither contested the suit nor preferred the appeal attributed to her. The application thus seeks reopening of an appellate adjudication. Its allocation follows the character of the proceedings sought to be reopened, and the application for restoration is incidental to that challenge. Dismissal for non-prosecution does not alter that character. The present applications, therefore, fall within Section 13(1)(b) of the Act and are to be dealt with by the designated Special Bench of this Court. The reference to that provision in the transmitting letter records the basis of transfer. The applicant’s concern regarding loss of a forum cannot alter that allocation. Any remedy against the eventual decision shall be governed by the applicable law. The objection to this Court entertaining the transferred proceedings is accordingly overruled.

7. Learned counsel for the respondent has expressly raised no objection to restoration. The present civil miscellaneous application is accordingly allowed, and the application under Section 12(2), CPC is restored to its original position. Its maintainability and merits, including the grounds of fraud pleaded therein, remain open for determination after hearing the parties. Relist. (ANWAAR HUSSAIN)
